highlights.title: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
highlights.summary: Meta is making another push to bring artificial intelligence to the masses with Muse, a personal assistant it says can put AI in the hands of virtually anyone. The product is the latest step in a multi-billion dollar strategy overhaul designed to revitalize the company's ailing position in the AI…
body: Meta drills down on ease of use and privacy options after spending billions overhauling its AI strategy.

Muse is a “personal AI agent” designed to help out with everyday tasks and projects, like online shopping, sending emails, and planning a trip. Once given a goal, Meta says Muse can work on its own, opening a browser, filling out forms, and even negotiating on users’ behalf. For lengthy tasks, Meta says Muse will continue working in the background after users close the app, returning to users if something changes or if it requires approval for something, such as making a purchase.

Muse will roll out in the US on iOS, Android, and muse.ai, with AI glasses “coming soon.” The assistant will be free for most users, though Meta said there will be paid subscriptions “for people who want to do more.” The company did not specify the nature and costs of these paid plans, nor outline what limits there are for free users.
“Muse is a first step: an agent that takes on more of the work so people can focus on what matters to them,” Meta said.

highlights.title: OpenAI Just Claimed a Huge Math Discovery. Some Academics Are Crying Foul
highlights.summary: A landmark announcement by the frontier AI lab has been overshadowed by accusations of impropriety.
body: OpenAI said today that it has found an AI-generated solution to one of the biggest problems in mathematics —a 200-year-old equation that describes the natural behavior of fluids like water and air.

The announcement appears to demonstrate the stunning power for AI to advance mathematics. But it has been marred by claims from another mathematician, Tristan Buckmaster, who says that OpenAI rushed ahead to solve the problem after learning of the work of Buckmaster and a colleague—Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge. Buckmaster claims OpenAI also tried to influence who got credit for the work.
The proof concerns the Navier-Stokes equation, one of the unsolved problems in the Clay Millennium prizes, which are each worth $1 million.
Sebastien Bubeck, a mathematician and AI researcher at OpenAI, said in a press briefing that the company began training a new AI model with advanced mathematical capabilities on August 28.

highlights.title: Aston Villa attack clicks in thrilling win over Club Brugge
highlights.summary: Aston Villa produced a superb attacking display to end their scoring concerns and begin their Champions League campaign with a thrilling 3-2 win over Club Brugge.
body: The Europa League winners had failed to score in their first three Premier League matches, having had just one shot on target, but their attack clicked in Belgium as John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Nicolas Jackson struck to kickstart their season.

Villa had 14 efforts in a scintillating first-half performance that began with McGinn expertly side-footing a trademark first-time shot into the bottom left corner after being set up by Pau Torres' driving run out of defence.

Club Brugge's expansive approach contributed to a breathless tie and the hosts equalised when Hugo Vetlesen swept a low shot into the corner, although Buendia restored Villa's lead within three minutes, tapping in from close range following good work by Joao Gomes.

Villa threatened constantly on the counter-attack and their third goal came when Jackson ran in behind to try and latch onto Torres' long ball forward, beating goalkeeper Yann Sommer to the ball and slotting into an empty net for his first goal since joining in a club-record £65m move.

highlights.title: Marvel's Ex-Blade Director Finally Made the Mahershala Ali Movie of His Dreams
highlights.summary: This did not impede Tariq from living the dream. Out of the ashes of Blade comes Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, a riveting, often spectral drama about a Muslim contract killer fighting to protect his children and provide for his newborn baby.
body: In 2021, director Bassam Tariq got the call of a lifetime: Marvel Studios wanted him to direct Blade. The indie filmmaker behind Riz Ahmed’s hip-hop drama Mogul Mowgli jumped at the chance to resurrect the vampire hunter with Oscar-winner Mahershala Ali ( Moonlight ) as the daywalker. But the dream never happened; by 2022, Tariq had departed the film, which then languished in development only to be dropped from Marvel’s future slate entirely.

Ahead of Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother ’s world premiere at the 2026 Toronto Film Festival and its Sept. 25 release date, I had a chance to speak to Tariq about crafting such a personal film that doubles as an adrenaline rush. You bet your ass Shenmue came up in conversation with a filmmaker whose inspirations range from video games to Lynne Ramsay and his own life as a parent.

Polygon: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is a movie where the director and lead actor feel in perfect sync, then drop a hammer on the audience. How would you describe your connection with Mahershala Ali going into this?

highlights.title: Godzilla Minus Zero IMAX trailer teases King Ghidorah
highlights.summary: One of the cinematic highlights of 2023 was director Takashi Yamazaki's gloriously grounded kaiju epic, Godzilla Minus One, which became a major international hit and snagged an Oscar for best visual effects. Yamazaki is back this fall with the hotly anticipated sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero.
body: Godzilla Minus One focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima, who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. Knocked unconscious, Kōichi woke to find he was one of only two survivors—and the other, a mechanic named Tachibana, was furious about it. His parents and many others were killed in the WWII bombing of Tokyo. Kōichi rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko and the orphaned baby she rescued, Noriko. But then Godzilla re-emerged, and Kōichi resolved to die fighting the monster to atone for Odo Island.

War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant. There is no third time. Everything ends here.

highlights.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: A predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
highlights.summary: AlphaGenome Atlas maps the molecular effects of 9 billion single-letter DNA variants across the human genome.
body: How predicting the molecular impact of every possible single-letter DNA variant in the human genome will help accelerate our understanding of biology.

Today, we are introducing AlphaGenome Atlas: a platform containing predictions for the effects of 9 billion single-nucleotide variants — every single-letter change possible — in the human genome. It is the most comprehensive catalogue of how genetic mutations affect molecular biology, and it is available for academic research through an intuitive and free-to-use website portal.

DNA is the language of life. Mastering it is a grand challenge that could transform our ability to understand biology and treat disease. But progress has been limited by a fundamental problem: interpreting how genetic variations impact biology at a molecular level. With roughly 9 billion possible single-letter mutations in the human genome, testing each one in the lab is practically impossible.
points: AlphaGenome Atlas maps the molecular effects of 9 billion single-letter DNA variants across the human genome.

highlights.title: Sabalenka survives Noskova battle to keep US Open three-peat bid alive
highlights.summary: Aryna Sabalenka maintained her hopes of a third successive US Open title with a three-set victory over Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in an absorbing quarter-final - a result that retains her status as world No 1 for at least one more day.
body: The 28-year-old beat Noskova 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7), coming through two tie-breaks - and a 4-2 deficit in the final set - as she sealed victory with a second-serve ace to set up a meeting with the winner of Tuesday night's all-American clash between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro in the semi-finals.

Sabalenka needs to win in New York to have any hope of staying as world No 1 but will definitely lose that spot if Elena Rybakina - who defeated Sabalenka in this year's Australian Open final - overcomes Qinwen Zheng in her quarter-final on Wednesday.
If Rybakina is beaten, then Pegula or Coco Gauff could rise to the top of the rankings should they win the tournament at Flushing Meadows on Saturday evening.
Sabalenka, world No 1 for 99 consecutive weeks, is hoping to become the first woman to win the US Open three times in a row since Serena Williams from 2012-14.

“Drunk History” started in 2007 as a Funny or Die web series before Comedy Central picked it up as a TV show that ran for six seasons from 2013 to 2019. highlights.title: The rise of hairy young women: ‘I know people who dye their armpit hair, so it stands out more’
highlights.summary: When Phoebe Bridgers appeared at Venice international film festival with unshaven legs this weekend, it shouldn’t have made headlines – but did. What do young women make of the current expectations around depilation? In 2026, female body hair feels as if it should be the least of anyone’s concerns.
body: Even so, her au naturel look may signal that attitudes are changing – particularly among younger generations. Vogue decreed that “rather than undermining the femininity of the look, unapologetic hair sharpened it”, and pictures of the 32-year-old’s hair-covered calves were generally praised by fans. But what do other gen Z and millennial women make of the decision to ditch the razor?

“Hell yeah!” is 27-year-old PhD student Anna Busuttil’s response. “I think it’s awesome; cool and rebellious,” she says – a view that chimes with that of most of the women I speak to outside University College London’s Bloomsbury campus. Busuttil says she sees a lot more women nowadays choosing not to remove their body hair. “I know people who dye their armpit hair a certain colour as well, so it stands out even more. I feel like leg hair is more taboo for women; it feels like such a ‘masculine’ thing, and legs are supposed to be a really sexy part of a woman.”

highlights.title: “This is the AI men actually use”: Meta ads pushed apps nudifying real teens
highlights.summary: Meta took days to remove ads containing AI-generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on Facebook and Instagram. Some ads featured photos of real kids, including a press photo of a young member of a European royal family and images swiped from a popular Instagram profile of a preteen girl deemed…
body: In an investigation published Tuesday, the Tech Transparency Project (TTP) reported that Meta failed to detect 332 ads containing CSAM this year. The “vast majority” of ads promoted AI apps made in China, while many ads promoted so-called “nudify” apps that make it easy for bad actors to use AI and digitally alter images of children.

TTP matched “multiple CSAM ads to photos of real children that appeared online.” These ads seem to violate federal child pornography laws, since the Justice Department has clarified that AI CSAM is just as harmful as CSAM. The young royal’s image was “animated into a video of her performing a graphic sex act,” TTP found. Other ads animated a photo of a 14-year-old Instagram influencer “showing off her new sports club uniform” into “a video of her performing oral sex.” A third “preteen” victim “posing in a pink athletic outfit with pigtails” in a series of stock photos was morphed into a video where she looks frightened as she’s molested by an adult male, TTP reported.

highlights.title: Google’s Atlas of the human genome could pave the way for new treatments
highlights.summary: Google DeepMind has unveiled an AI tool that its scientists claim could help unravel the mysteries of the human genome and transform our understanding of biology, accelerating scientific research and ultimately paving the way for new treatments for diseases.
body: DeepMind’s new AI-powered tool can learn patterns between DNA changes and our biology.
The platform, called AlphaGenome Atlas, contains a “predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome,” the researchers said in a blog post published on Tuesday.

DNA is written in an alphabet of four chemical “letters” — usually shortened to A, C, G, and T — and the human genome contains roughly three billion letter pairs. Those letters contain the instructions that make life work, such as how, when, and where genes are switched on and off, and to what degree. Changes to individual letters can be harmless, contribute to ordinary differences between people, or play a role in disease – a major challenge is figuring out which changes matter and how. It is a tough task as there are roughly nine billion potential single-letter substitutions.

highlights.title: Official GTA 6 Release Time Could Mean Long Waits for Some Players
highlights.summary: The PlayStation Store may offer official new details on the release timings for Grand Theft Auto 6 across multiple regions, revealing that Rockstar Games may have a staggered launch for its upcoming sequel.
body: Polygon has reached out to Rockstar for confirmation on the matter, but as of now, it seems that Grand Theft Auto 6 won't roll out simultaneously in all territories. The game will reportedly become available at 12 a.m. local time in each region, resulting in players across the world accessing it at different times, based on PlayStation Store data.

A staggered release may look bad at first glance, but it means that some fans can cheat the system and technically play it early. Xbox players can easily change their console's region to New Zealand and access the game as soon as 12 a.m. NZDT hits. As for the PlayStation release, accounts are region-locked, making this process much more complicated. It's unclear at this stage if Rockstar can convince Sony to change how it handles region-based rollouts.

To play GTA 6 early on PlayStation, users will have to make a new PlayStation account and set its region to New Zealand. On top of this, they'd have to play the game on this account rather than their main account because Grand Theft Auto 6 is region-locked on PlayStation.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X on Nov. 19.

highlights.title: Jibby Beane obituary
highlights.summary: My glamorous friend Jibby Beane, who has died aged 84, was known in London’s fashion and art worlds as an energetic and unique figure. Blessed with fabulous blond good looks, during the 1990s she appeared on the catwalk for Vivienne Westwood, was featured in countless style magazines and ran an art…
body: Wherever Jibby arrived, laced into a Westwood corset and tottering on platform shoes, everyone knew who she was. She had started modelling in the 60s and appeared in the first Andrex television commercial to feature a labrador retriever puppy in 1972. She had also worked for the couturier Victor Stiebel. In 1963 she married Kenneth Beane, whom she had known since childhood.

Talented at decorating houses, and selling them, she studied interior design and got a diploma from Richmond Adult College in the late 80s. She went on to establish her own company, Dream Designs, and worked occasionally at the Design and Decoration Building in Chelsea, where she was a greeter; there she met Westwood in the ladies’ loos. She had also met a young art student, Jonathan Goslan, in 1991, which led to her separation from Ken.

By 1992, Jibby was the face of Westwood’s Mayfair stores, holding court every Saturday as she slipped into one outfit after another. “She seemed to have multiple sides – from diva to comedian,” said Mark Garcia, a colleague. “But my favourite was the one she called ‘Mother Beane’. If you needed advice, or comfort, or reassurance, she would give it all. She was incredibly kind.”

highlights.title: Apple and Google Miss Deadline to Block Child Nudity on Their Phones in the UK
highlights.summary: Now the UK government plans to introduce new legislation that would see companies face fines and potential criminal liability, and signaled similar plans could extend to Snapchat and Instagram.
body: In June, the UK government told Big Tech it had three months to make taking, viewing, or sharing images of child nudity on their devices impossible. “I expect tech firms to make that happen,” said then prime minister Keir Starmer. “But if they choose not to, then we will act and change the law.”

That deadline arrived on Tuesday, and the government says that the likes of Apple and Google have failed. As a result, they will be changing the law to introduce what the UK government claims will be world-first legislation of its kind.

While engineers from Apple and Google had been working with the government since June to make changes, “they do not meet the scale of this crisis,” Lisa Nandy, the secretary of state for digital, culture, media, and sport, told lawmakers on Tuesday as she introduced the legislation.

Under the new plan, companies failing to build the child protection solutions into all existing and newly sold smartphones and tablets in the UK would face fines and potential criminal liability for their bosses. “We know that this is a sector that can—when required—innovate at an extraordinary pace when the chips are down,” Nandy added.
points: Now the UK government plans to introduce new legislation that would see companies face fines and potential criminal liability, and signaled similar plans could extend to Snapchat and Instagram.

highlights.title: Adobe is trying to make its AI generators idiot-proof in Premiere
highlights.summary: Adobe is overhauling how editors interact with AI in its Premiere professional video editing software. Its new Generative Media tool makes it easier to generate video, sound effects, music, and soundscapes without ever leaving the project timeline.
body: A dedicated Generative Media interface can now be accessed right from the project timeline.

Instead of jumping between browsers or external apps to find missing B-roll or audio elements, editors can now highlight an empty gap on the video or audio track and generate context-aware, fully editable clips without leaving the project. Editors can choose from multiple underlying models directly in the timeline — including Adobe Firefly, Google Veo, Runway, Luma, and Kling — to best match their project’s style.

Premiere is also getting new AI audio tools (in beta) that can separate overlapping speakers, automatically duck music under speech, and independently adjust dialogue and ambience. And Adobe is bringing its AI Assistant to After Effects (also in beta) that lets editors use plain-language commands to reorganize projects, fix technical problems, and create effects without writing expressions themselves.

highlights.summary: The cookbook author has a shortcut method for blanching vegetables that saves on time, equipment and water. Check out more Alice Zaslavsky recipes. I love a burnt brassica, and there’s no better flavour than the big mama herself: the cabbage.
body: Vegetables in the cruciferous family, like brussels sprouts, broccoli and cauliflower, have naturally bitter compounds. However, with concentrated heat, this bitterness is transformed into sweetly caramelised corners and burnished bits.
It’s one way to make brassica boo-ers braver. But getting cooked-through cabbage with a softened heart and gnarly edges requires a delicate balance of time under heat.

Lucky for us, the sharp bitterness of cabbage has been bred out of more conventional styles on supermarket and greengrocer shelves. Modern varieties are much milder, sweeter and less fibrous, meaning they require far less cooking than the cabbages of old.
That’s why these days, I’m fond of a gentler method that softens their rawness without overcooking: the kettle-blanch.

highlights.title: Update to Google’s AI weather model improves forecast accuracy
highlights.summary: Google is one of the major players in AI (meaning machine learning) weather forecast model space. The models it and others generate have their strengths and weaknesses, but the main advantage is that they can have forecast performance similar to traditional models while requiring far less computing…
body: Google recently released version 3 of its WeatherNext model, with the biggest change being that it now ingests some satellite weather data, shortening the lag time between current weather conditions and generating a new forecast. The update is detailed in a white paper.

Many weather models make use of what’s called a “reanalysis,” which is a sort of model of its own. Reanalyses take in all kinds of weather data and combine them into a single, consistent global snapshot of the atmosphere. That requires that they provide estimates for conditions over locations without real-world measurements, because weather forecast models need to work with a global picture.

Nearly all AI weather models have been relying entirely on reanalyses, with machine-learning algorithms training on global reanalyses and spitting out a weather map in the same format. There are some compromises there—the raw data sources themselves may contain some information that gets lost in the reanalysis blender, and these global snapshots are generally only produced every six hours.
points: Google is one of the major players in AI (meaning machine learning) weather forecast model space.

highlights.title: Shift Up CTO Clarifies Stellar Blade Developer's Stance on AI After Blood Rain Music Video Controversy
highlights.summary: Shift Up’s chief technology officer, DongKi Lee, has clarified the developer’s stance on AI after a music video for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain sparked backlash last month.
body: The music video, set to an upbeat pop song titled "Wanna be in Love," featured AI-generated images and footage that focused on Blood Rain’s main character, Evie, as she sang, danced, and made her way through the game’s futuristic world.

The public response was far from positive; players instantly lashed out at Shift Up for eschewing human employees in favor of having AI make the video, criticisms that the developer’s CEO, Kim Hyung Tae, argued against.

"EVIE, the character at the heart of this video, was created from head to toe by our talented artists and modelers through more than a year of dedicated work. The AI is not creating her from scratch. It is rendering and presenting the character based on the data, designs, and craftsmanship our team created. We would truly appreciate it if you could view the work with that understanding in mind," he wrote.

Shift Up’s CTO has now shed a bit more light on the situation now that tensions have cooled. In a September 2 interview with TheGamer, Lee explained that the company merely wanted to show off more of Evie’s world with its AI music video, and clarified that such content is "experimental" and not a reflection of the official game.
points: Shift Up’s chief technology officer, DongKi Lee, has clarified the developer’s stance on AI after a music video for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain sparked backlash last month.

Soft serve margaritas took over TikTok this year. And if line culture is any indication of interest, soft serve spots like Culture and, in my neighborhood, Lisbonata, now draw round-the-block throngs of treat seekers.

Rather than spending hours (and a small fortune) waiting in line, I decided to see if I could spin up some decent soft serve in my own kitchen. Enter Dash, a budget appliance brand known for its $11 mini waffle makers. I decided to try its line of ultra-affordable frozen dessert machines: the Soft Serve Ice Cream Maker, Deluxe Gelato & Ice Cream Maker and compact My Mug.

highlights.title: A new class action lawsuit questions whether Anthropic broke the law by misleading power users
highlights.summary: Anthropic says power users are key to its business - it's prioritized them even when it means cutting off other popular applications, like OpenClaw. But some of these same customers say Anthropic misled them into believing they'd get more out of a top-tier pricing subscription than they did.
body: Anthropic’s Max plan for Claude is an upgrade to the $20/month Pro plan. It has two pricing options: $100 per month for “5x” the usage limits of Pro or $200 per month for “20x”. But the lawsuit alleges that these numbers, advertised in Anthropic’s marketing graphics, are misleadingly couched in fine print. Anthropic actually says you’ll get 20x or 5x the usage that the Pro plan offers, but it’s only promised for five-hour chunks of time that are subject to a weekly limit — which the complaint alleges adds up to a much smaller total increase in usage capacity.

To understand this, “you’ve got to dive deep,” Vaca said. It requires clicking two different hyperlinks to see the word “session,” and then to see what “session” meant, you’d need to separately go to the Pro plan webpage for an expanded definition.

Complaints about Max’s terms have cropped up online. One Reddit user wrote, “The weekly allowance is what the pricing page makes you think you’re buying. The rolling 5-hour window is what actually controls whether you can work … It’s like giving someone a bigger gas tank while keeping the fuel pump limited to one gallon every five hours.”
points: Anthropic says power users are key to its business - it's prioritized them even when it means cutting off other popular applications, like OpenClaw.
But some of these same customers say Anthropic misled them into believing they'd get more out of a top-tier pricing subscription than they did.

highlights.title: OpenAI fought dirty on career-making math problem, says NYU mathematician
highlights.summary: There is a $1 million bounty for the first person providing a solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem.
body: NYU mathematics professor Tristan Buckmaster announced three proofs on Tuesday with a preliminary finding on one of the major unsolved problems in theoretical mathematics. The findings, made in collaboration with Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and using both Codex and Claude AI models, are significant in themselves — but they’re also accompanied by an unusual controversy surrounding OpenAI’s attempts to solve the same problem.

“There is another part of this story,” Buckmaster wrote in his statement announcing the proofs, “and one that, honestly, I very much wish I did not have to be concerned with.” According to the statement, a parallel effort by OpenAI built on their work before it became public, leading to a tangle of academic rivalries and conflicting claims.

highlights.title: Air traffic chaos delays Arsenal flight to Naples for Champions League
highlights.summary: Team arriving late at their hotel in southern Italy. Jurriën Timber in squad for first time since May. Arsenal’s preparations for their opening Champions League game against Napoli have been disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos that affected airports across the United Kingdom.
body: Mikel Arteta was forced to cancel his pre-match press conference at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Tuesday after Arsenal’s flight was severely delayed by an air-traffic control issue. The Arsenal manager and his players are understood to have remained at the club’s training ground in Hertfordshire as they waited for the delay to pass after completing their morning session as usual.

Club sources have insisted there has been no alteration to their planned schedule other than arriving later than expected to the team hotel. Uefa has also agreed to allow Arsenal to cancel their mandatory press conference due to the delays, which have also affected supporters travelling to Italy for the match.

Jurriën Timber is set to be part of the Arsenal squad for the first time since the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on 30 May after recovering from a groin injury. The Netherlands defender missed the World Cup due to the problem that has dogged him since March but Arteta said before Sunday’s win over Chelsea that Timber was close to returning.

highlights.title: Nintendo Doesn't Care About GTA 6
highlights.summary: Nintendo has gone ahead and broken a commandment that the mainstream video game industry seemed to have imposed on itself for 2026: thou shalt not release a game in the same month as Grand Theft Auto 6.
body: As it stands, Nintendo is the only major publisher willing to take a chance on a November release date (unless you count Sega/Atlus' release of the Switch 2 version of Metaphor: ReFantazio on Nov. 12). Most of the competition has crammed itself into September and October; a few games will see the light of day in early December, including strategy sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 and Nintendo's own re-release of Xenoblade Chronicles 3.

GTA 6 's blast radius has been agreed by some kind of industry consensus for a while, and Nintendo is showing some daring by stepping into it. There's no question that it's a risk. Go too soon after GTA 6, and a colossal portion of the gaming audience will be otherwise occupied; too soon before, and gamers will have earmarked their time and disposable income already.

Nintendo, however, doesn't seem to care. The company loves to give the impression that it is blithely unconcerned with what the rest of the gaming world is up to, but I'm sure that's not the case. So what gives it the confidence to sidle so close to what's expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time — confidence that nobody else in the game industry seems to have?

body: The LG Smart TVs we've tested have first-party ACR (automatic content recognition) functionality that can pry into your personal life with greater precision than you might realize, with LG Ad Solutions' executives and leadership saying, on camera, that LG "owns the glass." Not you -- even though you bought it -- but them. They also talk about knowing everybody in the household, knowing the secondary devices, moving from TVs to smartphones and other screens, and more in their B2B discussions. Beyond just the fact that we think the TV's native behavior parallels malware, the LG Smart TVs we tested also have a number of security vulnerabilities that can be exploited to convert the TVs into covert listening devices. In this investigation, we dive into the mix of LG's first-party functionality that (in our opinions) is tantamount to spying and LG's vulnerabilities and exploits that they have failed to protect against.
